sources.title: Evgeny Spodarev, Spatial Statistics: Lecture Notes (2024)
sources.locator: Focused complete Sections2.1–2.3, PDF pp.16–24 (printed pp.14–22), including Lemma2.14 on PDF24. Exact owner retrieval/reading and source fixed-grid target correction are recorded separately in the spatial spectral resolution.

contents.name: Example 2.1 uniform spatial-window mean and Lemma 2.2 unbiasedness
contents.reason: The carrier adopts the uniform Lebesgue window average and places its exact unbiasedness argument in the local L2 theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 2.3 covariance double-integral formula and Theorem 2.5 L2 consistency
contents.reason: The item proves the overlap form of the covariance double integral and uses the Van Hove boundary ratio with the stated absolute-integrability hypothesis.

contents.name: Section 2.2 pair-count covariance estimator and Lemma 2.8 asymptotic unbiasedness
contents.reason: The item retains the raw pair-product minus squared global mean convention and proves the finite lattice expectation limit under L2 mean consistency.

contents.name: Section 2.2 increment-based empirical semivariogram
contents.reason: The carrier defines the finite lag-pair difference-square estimator and proves its exact expectation under stationary second moments of increments.

contents.name: Definition 2.9 and Lemma 2.10 expected periodogram and Fejer convolution
contents.reason: The carrier rederives the finite-square identity for the sampled lattice spectral measure on the dual torus; it does not use the notes' continuous-space density as an unaliased fixed-grid target.

contents.name: Lemma 2.14 smoothing-kernel bias limit
contents.reason: The carrier proves the joint Fourier-grid bandwidth condition directly for its normalized kernel weights rather than importing the notes' iterated-limit argument.

contents.name: Subsequent variance, weak-consistency and central-limit claims for spectral estimators
contents.reason: The controlling SME-46 contract explicitly excludes periodogram variance consistency, weak consistency and central limit theorems, so these later claims are not part of the authored inventory.

contents.name: Definition2.9(b) fixed-spacing sampling and Lemma2.10(b) periodic-kernel integral, with local alias-target correction
contents.reason: Countable frequency-cell partition derives the full sampled alias identity; the source unaliased conclusion is not assumed.

contents.name: Unaliased physical-frequency bias under zero noncentral aliases; compactly supported Nyquist spectrum sufficient case
contents.reason: Locally proves the precise condition needed to recover the source intended unaliased value while preserving unrestricted lattice targets.

sources.title: Dennis Sun, Stanford Stats 253 Lecture 6: Covariance Estimation (2014)
sources.locator: Complete relevant covariance and variogram-estimation unit, PDF pp. 8–15: pair-lag sample covariance formula, the caution that the estimate need not be a valid covariance function, and the increment-based sample semivariogram formula.

contents.name: Regular-spacing pair-lag covariance estimator and irregular-spacing binning contrast
contents.reason: The regular-grid pair-lag convention is adopted; binning irregular locations is outside this pair's lattice estimator definition.

contents.name: Increment-square sample semivariogram estimator
contents.reason: The carrier specifies the finite pair set and normalization and proves the expectation identity under stationary increments.

contents.name: An empirical covariance estimate need not be a valid covariance function
contents.reason: The source supplies the caution; the B item gives its own exact finite data vector and negative quadratic-form witness.

contents.name: Parametric covariance or variogram fitting procedures
contents.reason: SME-46 defines estimators and proves only their stated expectation properties; it does not include model fitting algorithms or guarantees.

sources.title: Oxford Mathematical Institute, Harmonic Analysis lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete relevant character-identification unit, PDF pp. 17–18, Section 2.1: bounded characters of Z^d are the coordinatewise unit-circle powers, identifying the dual with the d-torus.

contents.name: Character group of Z^d identified with the d-torus
contents.reason: The local lemma states and proves the full group and compact-open topologies using evaluation on standard lattice basis vectors.

contents.name: Characters and Fourier analysis on R^d and the continuous torus
contents.reason: The local periodogram is defined for lattice-indexed observations on the dual torus; continuous-space Fourier estimation is not identified with that lattice target.

contents.name: Discrete lattice topology and group structure used for the Z^d dual
contents.reason: The local lemma proves the discrete locally compact Hausdorff abelian group interface used by the lattice dual and Bochner arguments.
